title: Ring of an affine singleton product
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $U,W$ affine objects of its small etale site, and $g:W\to U$ a morphism [new-etale-affine-singleton-tensor-degree-comparison-hom-normalization]. For $n\in\mathbf N$ let $P$ be the product of $n+1$ copies of $W$ over $U$, let $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, $B=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, and $C=\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)$, with algebra structures induced by the structure maps. Then $P$ is affine and there is an $A$-linear equivalence $\bigotimes_{k\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1),A} B\cong C$ taking an indexed pure tensor $(b_k)_k$ to $\prod_k\pi_k^*(b_k)$, where $\pi_k:P\to W$ is the $k$-th projection.

proof.text: Convert the product cone in Over U to a wide-pullback cone with Over.ConstructProducts.conesEquiv. The functor Etale.forget X composed with Over.forget X preserves this finite connected limit. Its vertices are U.left and the copies of W.left, all affine by the hypotheses. Apply Mathlib Scheme.isAffine_of_isLimit to prove affineness of the product.

Construct the wide-pushout cocone on the indexed tensor power: its base map is algebraMap and its factor maps are PiTensorProduct.singleAlgHom. For any competing cocone, its base map equips the vertex with an A-algebra structure, and cocone compatibility makes the factor maps A-algebra homomorphisms. PiTensorProduct.liftCommAlgHom supplies the unique map from the tensor power. Its singleAlgHom formula proves factorization and PiTensorProduct.algHom_ext proves uniqueness. This establishes the colimit universal property directly in Lean, in the private tensorCoconeIsColimit construction.

Mathlib preservesLimit_rightOp_Γ sends the affine wide-pullback limit cone to a limit in opposite commutative rings, hence a colimit cocone in commutative rings. Identify its diagram with the algebraMap diagram by WidePullbackShape.functorExt. Compare this colimit with the tensor-power cocone to obtain a ring isomorphism. The cocone identity at the base proves preservation of A-scalars, giving an A-algebra equivalence and then the stated linear equivalence. The identities at the factor vertices and PiTensorProduct.algHom_ext identify its map with liftCommAlgHom of the projection pullbacks; liftCommAlgHom_tprod gives the required product formula. This covers n = 0 and the zero-ring case without additional hypotheses.

lean.statement:
theorem singletonProduct_affine_ring
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U W : X.Etale) (g : W ⟶ U)
    (hU : IsAffine U.left) (hW : IsAffine W.left) (n : ℕ) :
    letI : Algebra Γ(U.left, ⊤) Γ(W.left, ⊤) := g.left.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
    let P := ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Over.mk g)
    letI : Algebra Γ(U.left, ⊤) Γ(P.left.left, ⊤) := P.hom.left.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
    IsAffine P.left.left ∧
      ∃ e : (⨂[Γ(U.left, ⊤)] (_ : Fin (n + 1)), Γ(W.left, ⊤)) ≃ₗ[Γ(U.left, ⊤)]
        Γ(P.left.left, ⊤),
        ∀ b : Fin (n + 1) → Γ(W.left, ⊤),
          e (PiTensorProduct.tprod Γ(U.left, ⊤) b) =
            ∏ k : Fin (n + 1),
              (Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Over.mk g) k).left.left.appTop (b k)
